editorial:
Imagine being fifteen and feeling like your body is betraying you, but instead of just normal puberty, you are actually turning into a fish. You follow Mia, a lonely teen who starts noticing weird scales on her skin and a strange urge to be in the water. It feels like a scary dream where she tries to hide her changes from everyone, but the more she fights it, the harder it gets. The vibe is heavy and moody, making you feel exactly how confused and scared she is as she realizes she is not human at all.

What really works here is the acting; the lead girl makes you feel every bit of her pain and fear. The movie moves a bit slow at times, but the practical effects look great and feel real. If you like stories about people changing into something else, you will love this. Since the visuals are so detailed, you should try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting it on Apple TV to see all the textures. If you are a big movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move.
endingExplained: At the end, Mia stops fighting her nature and fully gives in to the change. She transforms completely into a fish-like creature. She leaves her human life, her family, and her home behind to swim away into the deep ocean. The movie wraps up by showing that she finally found peace by accepting what she truly is, even though it meant losing her old identity and leaving the human world forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strange coming-of-age stories with a supernatural twist.
